In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new class of materials, MOFs with tunable thermal expansion, which can be used as a platform for controlling thermal expansion of devices, with a wide range of potential applications, from microelectronic to thermal management of energy.
a new concept for controlling thermal expansion in materials, which is based on the use of MOFs as platforms.
the development of a new strategy for designing materials that display thermal expansion behavior that can be controlled in a colligativistic way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adsorption–desorption of molecules of appropriate size and chemical nature can induce the thermal expansion of a solid to be either positive, zero, and/or negative.
the adsorbates, by changing the thermal expansion of a MOF, can induce the solid to display a positive, zero, and negative thermal expansion.
the thermal expansion of a MOF can be tuned by the adsorption of different guest species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adsorption of molecules in MOFs can be used to control the thermal expansion of materials in a wide range of temperatures.
MOF-5 is a good candidate to design a negative thermal expansion device, whereas MOF-5–methanol and MOF-5-1-butanol are good candidates for designing zero thermal expansion devices.

The main takeaway from our work is that
MOFs can be designed to display a wide range of thermal expansion properties, from positive to zero to negative thermal expansion, by simply changing the adsorbent molecules.
the thermal expansion of a MOF can be controlled by the adsorbate molecule, and that MOFs are a new class of materials with potential for thermal expansion control.
the adsorbate can control, in an additive way, the thermal behavior of the host MOF.
